body:
## Pull request overview

Fixes a `ReportView` crash in the console app caused by a render-time state sync race (`initialReport` defined before `reportData`) and aligns report display naming between `@objectstack/spec` (`label`) and the UI viewer (`title`), restoring CI test stability.

**Changes:**
- Strengthen `ReportView` render guards to avoid dereferencing `reportData` before it syncs.
- Add a boundary mapping from `label` → `title` when passing the report into `ReportViewer`, and add display fallbacks.
- Adjust `ReportView` integration tests to account for the title rendering in multiple places.

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 2 out of 2 changed files in this pull request and generated 4 comments.

| File | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| apps/console/src/components/ReportView.tsx | Prevents crash by guarding `reportData` availability and maps `label` → `title` for `ReportViewer`. |
| apps/console/src/__tests__/ReportView.test.tsx | Updates assertions to handle multiple title occurrences after the UI change. |

The new guard prevents the crash when `initialReport` resolves before `reportData`, but it still allows a stale `reportData` to render when the route param `reportName` changes (because both `initialReport` and `reportData` can be truthy while referring to different reports). Consider extending the guard to also check that `reportData.name === reportName` (or resetting `reportData` immediately on `reportName` change) so the UI doesn’t briefly show the previous report and trigger an extra data fetch.

`reportForViewer` maps `label -> title` only for `ReportViewer`, but `reportData` itself (and `ReportBuilder` in edit mode) will still see `title` as missing when metadata comes from `@objectstack/spec`. To avoid inconsistent behavior (e.g., the Report Builder title input appearing blank), consider normalizing the report shape once (when syncing state from `initialReport`) so `reportData.title` is always defined/fallbacks to `label` throughout this component.

Using `getAllByText(...)[0]` weakens the assertion: it now only checks that at least one occurrence exists, and won’t fail if the header or toolbar title stops rendering. Since the intent is that the title appears in both places, assert on the expected count (e.g., `toHaveLength(2)`) or target each location explicitly (e.g., `getByRole('heading', { level: 1, ... })` and `getByRole('heading', { level: 2, ... })`).
